notes: NCBI MedGen/GTR and NCBI Gene records were live and current on 2026-08-27.
Endotext current edition was verified in 2026; rare-endocrine-hypertension table directly supports the cortisol/cortisone discriminator.
NCBI Bookshelf/MedlinePlus differential sources were current when accessed.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.phenotype_and_primary_mechanism: NCBI MedGen/GTR defines AME as low-renin, low-aldosterone hypertension with hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis from HSD11B2 deficiency, reduced cortisol-to-cortisone conversion, and inappropriate cortisol activation of the mineralocorticoid receptor.
claim_audit.urinary_discriminator: Endotext Table 7 lists increased urinary free cortisol/cortisone and cortisol-metabolite ratios for AME, distinguishing it from Liddle syndrome and other rare low-renin hypertension syndromes.
claim_audit.hsd11b2_identity: NCBI Gene identifies HSD11B2 as 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 and links the gene to AME.
claim_audit.distractor_1: NCBI Liddle Syndrome supports gain-of-function ENaC with hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis and low renin/aldosterone but not impaired cortisol-to-cortisone metabolism.
claim_audit.distractor_2: Endotext Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia supports CYP11B1 deficiency causing DOC accumulation and low-renin hypertension with suppressed aldosterone.
claim_audit.distractor_3: Endotext/NCBI primary aldosteronism sources support autonomous aldosterone production with suppressed renin; the stem instead has suppressed aldosterone.
claim_audit.distractor_4: MedlinePlus PHA1 supports NR3C2/mineralocorticoid-receptor loss causing reduced sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion, yielding salt loss and hyperkalemia.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The phenotype is pseudomineralocorticoid excess. The increased urinary cortisol-to-cortisone ratio localizes the defect to failure of cortisol inactivation by renal 11-beta-HSD2, making AME the unique mechanism.
adversarial_second_pass.liddle_challenge: Liddle syndrome is the closest phenotype competitor because renin and aldosterone are also low; however ENaC gain of function does not increase the cortisol-to-cortisone ratio.
adversarial_second_pass.cyp11b1_challenge: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency uses DOC excess, not defective cortisol-to-cortisone conversion, and therefore does not explain the urinary steroid discriminator.
adversarial_second_pass.primary_aldosteronism_challenge: Autonomous aldosterone secretion would make aldosterone inappropriately high rather than suppressed.
adversarial_second_pass.mr_loss_challenge: Mineralocorticoid receptor loss causes the opposite renal phenotype—sodium wasting and hyperkalemia.
adversarial_second_pass.licorice_challenge: Licorice can inhibit 11-beta-HSD2 and phenocopy AME; the lead asks for the molecular defect rather than whether it is inherited or acquired, and the correct biochemical mechanism remains reduced 11-beta-HSD2 activity. No exposure history is required.
adversarial_second_pass.hidden_assumption_check: No dose, treatment, cutoff, inheritance assertion or unprovided exposure is necessary to answer.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five options are mechanistic explanations for renal/endocrine blood-pressure disorders and are of comparable specificity.
